newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Rebels say Sri Lanka's aim to end war unrealistic.
newsitem.headline: Rebels say Sri Lanka's aim to end war unrealistic.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Tamil Tiger rebels said on Monday that two attacks at the weekend in which 28 servicemen were killed should be a clear reminder to the government of their fighting capability.

The rebels' Voice of Tigers radio said the attacks on Sunday in the island's east disproved comments made the same day by Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte about ending the ethnic war this year.

"The attacks should prove that the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) can strike at will and are still capable of causing severe damage to the Sri Lankan military establishment," the radio said in a news broadcast.

The LTTE, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of the mainly Sinhalese nation, killed 22 soldiers and six policemen in separate attacks on an army patrol and a police post in eastern Trincomalee district.

The radio said two rebels were killed trying to stop reinforcements reaching the soldiers who came under attack while on a route clearing patrol at Pulmoddai, about 240 km (150 miles) east of the capital Colombo.
Ratwatte said security forces would "liberate" about 100,000 Tamil civilians living under rebel control in the northern Wanni region and finish the war before the end of this year.

His comments came during a speech he made to mark the opening of a police post at the village of Pariyanalankulam along the northern Vavuniya-Mannar road, captured from the rebels by security forces after a massive offensive in February.

Military officials said security forces were preparing for a major thrust into the rebel-held Wanni region, in a bid to link government-controlled Vavuniya, 220 km (138 miles) north of Colombo, with the Jaffna peninsula, some 100 km (60 miles) further north.
The government says more than 50,000 have died in the conflict, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the toll is much higher.
